text:
maya: sec-bot flagged a pod on prod-eu-west-1 that created /host/proc symlink and attempted to write /host/etc/ssh/authorized_keys. possible container escape.
sec-bot: DETECTION: host-bind-mount-write (pod: payment-processor-7f8c9) node=node-42 image=registry.redwood/internal/payproc:2.1.3 sha256:abcd1234 actions=recreate
jonas: seeing it, node-42 shows a hostPath mount / in the pod spec. grabbing pod YAML.
maya: pasted pod yaml:
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: payment-processor-7f8c9
spec:
  containers:
  - name: pay
    image: registry.redwood/internal/payproc:2.1.3
    volumeMounts:
    - mountPath: /host
      name: host-mnt
  volumes:
  - name: host-mnt
    hostPath:
      path: /
```
april: who created that deployment? looks like an infra job accidentally used hostPath / (uh)
jonas: owner tag says team=payments, iam serviceAccount=payments-runner
sre-liz: node cordoned, pod evicted. collecting node journal and container logs now.
maya: revoke payments-runner SA tokens, rotate deploy keys, and stop any active rollout. also check KMS usage for that workload.
security-ops: registry shows image manifest digest mismatch: manifest sha256:efgh5678 vs pulled sha256:abcd1234. opening registry incident.
april: any evidence of outbound network exfil? egress logs show a single conn to 18.23.45.67:443 at ~03:12 UTC from that pod's IP.
jonas: that IP listed in our TI as suspicious last month. pulling flow logs and firewall logs.
maya: containment checklist: 1) snapshot node (no reboot) 2) collect /proc, mounts, docker/socket artifacts 3) gather container logs and exec history 4) rotate SA creds 5) rotate KMS keys if used by pod.
auditor: we need kube-apiserver audit logs for 02:50-03:30 UTC, retention currently 7d — exporting now to secure S3.
maya: registry team: was cosign/enforced image signature enabled for internal/payproc?
security-ops: cosign signatures exist but digest doesn't match. enforcement is not enabled for this repo.
oncall: opened incident INC-2026-042 and a PagerDuty alert to sec-oncall. summary on the incident page.
april: recommend internal notification to SOC + product security. Legal not yet; customer impact unknown.
jonas: evidence so far: node snapshot, container rootfs diff, network flow to 18.23.45.67, registry digest mismatch. no indicators of lateral movement beyond that node.
sre-liz: uploaded node snapshot and collected logs to evidence bucket s3://redwood-evidence/1812345678/node42.tar.gz and s3://redwood-evidence/1812345678/pod-logs.tgz
maya: next actions: block the offending image tag, mark digest as malicious in registry denylist, enforce admission webhook to block hostPath:/ and hostNetwork, require RBAC approval for workloads requesting host mounts.
security-ops: creating vulnerability ticket in JIRA and tagging eng-runtime + registry + payments.
jonas: will run binary diff on image layers and compare to last known good digest. also scan image for suspicious binaries.
auditor: schedule post-incident review with timeline and privilege changes; need list of changed RBAC, SA rotations, KMS rotations.
maya: good work. assign follow-ups: ENG-RUNTIME (admission policy), REGISTRY (signature enforcement + denylist), PAYMENTS (service account review). postmortem required within 72h. :white_check_mark:
